# Peregrine Bastable

## Description
Tall, fretful, immaculate, with a clipboard of vellum and a watch on a chain he consults
every forty seconds. Carries a second clipboard for checking the first; the second
clipboard is also filled in. Hums the Midwinter reel without knowing it. Speaks to the party
the way one speaks to a draught: politely, while trying to find where it is coming from.

## Personality & motivation
A perfectionist who has planned this day for a year and will not have it spoiled by
foreigners, weather, or the King. He loves the crowning the way a conductor loves the
last bar. He would never cancel it, move it, or let anyone near the Crown; he would
sooner be hanged, and he says so, often. He is also, underneath, a frightened man who
has started to notice that his clipboard is already filled in.

## Knowledge & secrets
- Freely shares: the programme, to the minute (lottery 10:00; procession 20:00 from the square; the King enters the Hall 20:50; the crowning 21:00; feast until midnight); the Crown's five settings "are decorative"; the effigies were built by the carpenters "to my drawing"
- Needs persuasion (DC 14): the four empty settings were full yesterday. He is sure of it. He has a drawing. The drawing on the clipboard shows five stones and he does not remember making it
- Under duress (DC 16) or shown proof of the loop: he will admit his clipboard's every line was already ticked when he woke, in his own hand, and that he has been pretending all day that it was not. He then becomes very helpful, in a brittle way, and will stall the crowning by up to ten minutes with a speech
